q: Complete the series: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
why: Each term is a square minus 1 (2²−1, 3²−1, ... 6²−1), so next is 7²−1 = 48.

q: What comes next: 1, 8, 27, 64, ?
why: These are cubes: 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³, so next is 5³ = 125.
The gaps grow by 1: +1, +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6 gives 23.

q: Find the next number: 5, 10, 8, 16, 14, 28, ?
why: The rule alternates ×2 and −2. After 28 comes −2, giving 26.

q: Complete the series: 81, 27, 9, 3, ?
why: Each term is divided by 3, so 3 ÷ 3 = 1.
Double and add 1: 31 × 2 + 1 = 63.

q: What comes next: 2, 4, 8, 14, 22, ?
why: The gaps rise by 2: +2, +4, +6, +8, then +10 gives 32.

q: Find the next number: 4, 9, 19, 39, ?
why: Double and add 1: 39 × 2 + 1 = 79.
Multiply by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in turn, so next is 120 × 6 = 720 (factorials).

q: Complete the series: 0, 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, ?
why: Gaps are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, so next gap is 6: 15 + 6 = 21.
These are the prime numbers. After 13 the next prime is 17 (15 = 3 × 5).

q: What comes next: 1, 4, 10, 22, 46, ?
why: Double and add 2: 46 × 2 + 2 = 94.

q: Find the next number: 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, ?
why: The gaps double: 2, 4, 8, 16, then 32. 33 + 32 = 65.

q: Complete the series: 10, 9, 7, 4, 0, ?
why: The drops grow: −1, −2, −3, −4, then −5, so 0 − 5 = −5.
Double and add 1: 47 × 2 + 1 = 95.

q: What comes next: 6, 11, 21, 41, ?
why: Double and subtract 1: 41 × 2 − 1 = 81.

q: Find the next number: 1, 5, 14, 30, 55, ?
why: The gaps are square numbers: 4, 9, 16, 25, then 36. 55 + 36 = 91.

q: Complete the series: 5, 6, 8, 11, 15, 20, ?

why: The drops grow by 1: −1, −2, −3, −4, then −5 gives 85.

q: What comes next: 1, 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
why: Each term is a square plus 1 (0²+1, 1²+1, ... 5²+1), so next is 6²+1 = 37.

q: Find the next number: 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, 24, ?
why: Each term is the sum of the previous three: 7 + 13 + 24 = 44.
Each term is the last × 1.5. 27 × 1.5 = 40.5.

q: Complete the series: 21, 20, 18, 15, 11, ?
why: The drops grow: −1, −2, −3, −4, then −5. 11 − 5 = 6.

q: What comes next: 2, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5, ?
why: It is pairs counting up by 2, each written big then small: (2,1), (4,3), (6,5), (8,7).

q: Find the next number: 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 5, 4, ?
why: The pattern alternates +2 and −1. After 4 comes +2, giving 6.

q: Complete the series: 2, 4, 3, 9, 4, 16, 5, ?
why: Two interleaved lists: 2, 3, 4, 5 and the squares 4, 9, 16, 25.
The rule alternates −1 and ×2. After 13 comes ×2 = 26.
These are the digits of pi: 3.1415926...

q: Which letter comes next: A, C, F, J, O, ?
why: The gaps grow: +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6. O is the 15th letter; 21st is U.

q: Which letter completes it: Z, X, U, Q, ?
why: Counting backward with growing steps: −2, −3, −4, then −5. Q is 17th; 12th is L.

q: Continue the letters: A, D, H, M, S, ?
why: Steps grow: +3, +4, +5, +6, then +7. S is 19th; 26th is Z.

q: What comes next: M, V, E, M, J, S, U, ?
why: These are the first letters of the planets from the Sun: ... Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

q: Which pair comes next: AZ, BY, CX, ?
why: The first letter moves forward and the second moves backward: D and W.

q: Next in the letters: Z, A, Y, B, X, ?
why: Two interleaved lists: Z, Y, X backward and A, B, C forward.

q: Complete the pattern: A1, B4, C9, D16, ?
why: Letters go up in order and numbers are squares: 5² = 25.

q: A $80 jacket is marked up 25%, then discounted 25%. Final price?
why: $80 × 1.25 = $100, then 25% off $100 is $75. The percentages apply to different bases.

q: A price rises 10%, then falls 10%. Net change?
why: 1.10 × 0.90 = 0.99, so the price ends 1% lower.

q: What is 20% of 50% of 300?

why: Multiplication and division first: 6 + 1 + 36 = 43.

q: A film starts at 7:50 pm and runs 2 h 25 min. It ends at?
why: 7:50 + 2 h = 9:50, and 25 more minutes makes 10:15 pm.

q: How many minutes from 3:45 pm to 6:20 pm?
why: 3:45 to 6:00 is 135 minutes, plus 20 more is 155.

q: Take 40% off a price, then another 10% off. Total discount?
why: 0.60 × 0.90 = 0.54 remains, so the total discount is 46%.

q: What is 25% of 25% of 400?
If 8% of a number is 24, what is the number?
A $60 bill gets a 15% tip and is split 3 ways. Each pays?
Shirts are $12 each, buy 2 get the 3rd free. You take 6 shirts. Total?
why: Every third shirt is free, so you pay for 4: 4 × $12 = $48.

q: A car drives 30 min at 60 km/h, then 30 min at 40 km/h. Average speed?
why: Equal times, so the average is the mean: (60 + 40) ÷ 2 = 50.

q: You drive 60 km out at 30 km/h and back at 60 km/h. Average speed?
why: Out takes 2 h and back takes 1 h: 120 km in 3 h is 40 km/h.
Four thousands make 4000, and 40 + 30 + 20 + 10 = 100.

q: What is 50% more than 50% of 80?
why: 50% of 80 is 40, and 40 + half of 40 = 60.

q: How many times is the digit 9 written from 1 to 100?
why: Ones place: 9, 19, ... 99 is 10 times. Tens place: 90 to 99 is 10 more.
Multiply and divide first: 100 − 50 + 5 = 55.

q: A tank that is 1/4 full takes 30 L to reach 1/2 full. Capacity?
why: 30 L is 1/4 of the tank, so the capacity is 4 × 30 = 120 L.

q: What is 3/4 of 3/4 of 64?
why: 3/4 of 64 is 48, and 3/4 of 48 is 36.

q: 3 h 50 min plus 2 h 20 min equals?
why: 50 + 20 = 70 minutes, which is 1 h 10 min. 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 h, so 6 h 10 min.

q: What is 0.2 × 0.3?
why: 2 × 3 = 6, and two decimal places in total gives 0.06.

q: Which is greater: 40% of 50 or 50% of 40?
why: Both equal 20. Percent of a number is symmetric: a% of b = b% of a.

q: A stock falls 50%, then rises 50%. Compared to the start it is?
why: 100 → 50 → 75, which is 25% below the start.

q: Three back-to-back 30-minute tasks start at 11:45 am. They end at?
What is 1/2 ÷ 1/4?
why: Dividing by 1/4 means multiplying by 4: 1/2 × 4 = 2.

q: A $100 phone is 20% off, then $10 off. Final price?
why: 20% off gives $80, then $10 off gives $70.

q: What gets wetter the more it dries?
why: A towel dries you and so gets wetter itself.

q: What has hands but cannot clap?
why: A clock has hour and minute hands but cannot clap.

q: What goes up when the rain comes down?
why: An umbrella is raised as the rain falls.

q: A man pushes his car to a hotel and loses his fortune. Why?
why: He is playing the board game: the car token lands on a hotel property.

q: What can you break without ever touching it?
why: Promises are broken by what you do or fail to do, not by touch.

q: What can travel around the world while staying in a corner?
why: A postage stamp sits in the corner of an envelope while it travels.

q: What has one eye but cannot see?
why: A sewing needle has a single eye (the hole for thread). A potato has many.

q: How many animals of each kind did Moses take on the ark?
why: It was Noah, not Moses, who built the ark.

q: A plane crashes on the US-Canada border. Where are survivors buried?
why: Survivors are alive, so they are not buried.

q: You enter a dark room with a candle, a lamp and a fireplace, and one match. What first?
why: Nothing else lights until the match itself is lit.

q: Mary's father has five daughters: Nana, Nene, Nini, Nono and ...?
why: The fifth daughter is Mary, named at the start of the question.

q: A rooster lays an egg on a roof's peak. Which way does it roll?
why: Roosters do not lay eggs.

q: If a red house is made of red bricks, what is a greenhouse made of?
why: A greenhouse is a glass building for growing plants.

q: I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. What am I?
why: An echo repeats sound with no mouth or ears.

q: What 5-letter word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?
why: Short + er = shorter.

q: Pointing at a portrait, a man says: 'I have no siblings, but that man's father is my father's son.' Who is in the portrait?
why: 'My father's son' with no siblings is the speaker himself, so the portrait man's father is him. It is his son.

q: How can you drop a raw egg onto a concrete floor without cracking it?
why: The egg will break, but the concrete floor will not crack.

q: What occurs once in a minute, twice in a moment, never in a thousand years?
why: M appears once in 'minute', twice in 'moment', and not in 'a thousand years'.

q: Two fathers and two sons go fishing and catch 3 fish, one each. How many people?
why: A grandfather, his son, and his grandson: the middle one is both father and son.

q: The doctor's brother is called Sam, but Sam has no brother. How?
why: The doctor is Sam's sister, so Sam has a sister but no brother.

q: The more of me you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
why: Every step you take leaves another footstep behind.

q: What can you hold in your left hand but never in your right?
why: Your left hand can grab your right elbow, but your right hand can never reach it.

q: A brick weighs 1 kg plus half a brick. How much does the brick weigh?
why: If half a brick weighs 1 kg, the whole brick weighs 2 kg.

q: How many squares of any size are on a chessboard?
A book has pages numbered 1 to 100. How many digits are printed?
why: 9 one-digit pages, 90 two-digit pages (180 digits) and 3 digits for 100: 9 + 180 + 3 = 192.

q: What is the smallest number divisible by 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6?
why: 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 covers every factor; 30 is not divisible by 4.

q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 2:30?
why: The minute hand is at 180°, the hour hand halfway between 2 and 3 at 75°: 180 − 75 = 105.

q: Kim is taller than Lee, Lee is taller than Max, and Max is taller than Ned. Who is second shortest?
why: From tallest: Kim, Lee, Max, Ned. Max is second from the bottom.
Each term reads out the one before: 111221 is three 1s, two 2s, one 1 = 312211.

q: How many two-digit numbers have digits that add up to 5?
Odd one out: Whale, Dolphin, Shark, Seal
why: A shark is a fish; the others are mammals.

q: Odd one out: Spider, Ant, Beetle, Bee
why: Spiders have eight legs and are arachnids; the rest are six-legged insects.

q: Odd one out: Venus, Mars, Moon, Jupiter
why: The Moon is a satellite, not a planet.

q: Odd one out: Mercury, Iron, Copper, Granite
why: Granite is a rock; the others are metals.

q: Odd one out: Level, Radar, Civic, Planet
why: Planet does not read the same backward; the others are palindromes.

q: Which English word has three consecutive pairs of double letters?
why: B-oo-kk-ee-per has oo, kk and ee in a row.

q: Which number name has its letters in alphabetical order?
why: F-O-R-T-Y runs alphabetically. 'Four' fails because U comes after R.

q: Shift each letter of HAL one place forward in the alphabet. Result?
why: H→I, A→B, L→M gives IBM.

q: If A=1, B=2, C=3 and so on, what is the value of DEAD?
How many times does the letter S appear in MISSISSIPPI?
why: M-I-S-S-I-S-S-I-P-P-I has four S's.

q: Anna is twice Ben's age. In 6 years she will be 1.5 times his age. Ben is?
why: Now Anna 12, Ben 6. In 6 years: 18 and 12, and 18 = 1.5 × 12.

q: Today is Wednesday. What day is it 100 days from now?
why: 100 = 14 weeks + 2 days, so Wednesday + 2 = Friday.

q: Today is Monday. What day was it 10 days ago?
why: 10 days = 1 week + 3 days. Monday − 3 days is Friday.

q: Three days from now is Tuesday. What day was it two days ago?
why: Today is Saturday, so two days ago was Thursday.

q: One tap fills a bucket in 6 minutes, another in 3. Both together?
why: Rates add: 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 bucket per minute, so 2 minutes.

q: Two painters take 6 hours to paint a room. How long for three painters?
why: The job is 12 painter-hours. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 hours.

q: A snail climbs 3 m by day and slips 2 m at night. On which day does it exit a 10 m wall?
why: After 7 days it is at 7 m. On day 8 it climbs 3 m to the top before slipping.

q: A father is 30 years older than his son. In 5 years he is 4× his age. Son's age now?
why: Now 5 and 35. In 5 years: 10 and 40, and 40 = 4 × 10.

q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 3:15?
why: The minute hand is at 90°. The hour hand is a quarter past the 3, at 97.5°. The gap is 7.5°.

q: Tom has 3 sisters, and each sister has exactly 1 brother. How many children?
why: The one brother is Tom, so 3 sisters + Tom = 4.

q: Mia has 6 more coins than Joe. Together they have 36. Joe has?
why: Joe 15, Mia 21: 15 + 21 = 36 and the gap is 6.

q: A watch loses 6 minutes each hour. Set right at noon, it shows what at 3 pm?
why: It loses 3 × 6 = 18 minutes in 3 hours, so 3:00 − 0:18 = 2:42.

q: In 2 years Eve will be twice the age she was 4 years ago. Her age now?
why: Now 10: in 2 years she is 12, and 4 years ago she was 6, and 12 = 2 × 6.

q: It is Monday 10 am. What day and time will it be 53 hours later?
why: 48 hours later is Wednesday 10 am, and 5 more hours is 3 pm.

q: A rectangle is twice as long as it is wide, with perimeter 60. Its area?
why: Width 10, length 20: perimeter 60 and area 200.

q: Six people each shake hands once with every other person. Handshakes?
why: 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15, since each handshake is counted twice.

q: Which is larger: 3^4 or 4^3?
Which is largest: 5/8, 0.6, 62%, 3/5?
why: As decimals: 0.625, 0.6, 0.62, 0.6. So 5/8 is largest.
The others are perfect squares; 48 is not.

q: Which does not belong: 8, 27, 64, 100, 125
why: The others are cubes (2³, 3³, 4³, 5³); 100 is not.

q: Which does not belong: 14, 21, 35, 49, 52
why: The others are multiples of 7; 52 is not.
The others use the digits 1, 2, 3 and have digit sum 6. 124 has digit sum 7.

q: Which is bigger: 7 × 9 or 8 × 8?
Which is bigger: 99 × 101 or 100 × 100?
Which is bigger: 2/3 of 45 or 3/4 of 44?
why: 2/3 of 45 is 30 and 3/4 of 44 is 33.

q: Which is largest: 2^8, 3^5, 5^3, 11^2?
why: They are 256, 243, 125 and 121.

q: Which fraction is smallest: 3/4, 5/8, 7/12, 2/3?
why: As decimals: 0.75, 0.625, 0.583, 0.667. So 7/12 is smallest.

q: Which of these is not prime: 51, 53, 59, 61?
why: 51 = 3 × 17. The rest are prime.

q: 3 cards: red/red, white/white, red/white. You draw one and see a red side. Chance the other side is red?
why: There are 3 red faces you could be seeing; 2 of them belong to the red/red card.

q: Roll two dice. What is the chance that at least one shows a six?
why: No six on either die is 25/36, so at least one six is 1 − 25/36 = 11/36.

q: A drawer holds 10 black and 10 white socks. In the dark, how many must you take to be sure of 2 black?
why: Worst case you pull all 10 white first, then 2 more must both be black: 12.
That's the first 20 odd numbers, and the first n odd numbers add to n², so 20² = 400.
Each term is 1/n − 1/(n+1), so the sum collapses to 1 − 1/6 = 5/6.

q: How many zeros are at the end of 1 × 2 × 3 × … × 30?
why: Count factors of 5: 30 has six multiples of 5, and 25 adds one extra, so 7.

q: A says 'B lies.' B says 'C lies.' C says 'A and B both lie.' Who tells the truth?
why: If C were truthful, A lies, so B is truthful, a contradiction. So C lies, B is truthful and A lies.

q: Boxes labelled Apples, Oranges and Mixed are ALL mislabelled. Take one fruit from which box to fix every label?
why: The 'Mixed' box holds one fruit only, so one pick names it, and the other two labels then follow.

q: A two-digit number's digits add to 10. Reversed, it is 36 bigger. What is it?
why: Reversing changes it by 9 × (digit gap), so the gap is 4. Digits 3 and 7: 73 − 37 = 36.

q: Forward I'm heavy, but backward I'm not. What am I?
why: TON spelled backward is NOT.

q: Which word can be typed using only the top letter row (QWERTYUIOP) of a keyboard?
why: T, Y, P, E, W, R and I are all top-row letters. Printer needs N, Keyboard needs K, Computer needs C.

q: Which letter is 10 places after the letter that is 5 places before P?
why: 5 before P is K (11th letter). 10 after K is the 21st letter, U.

q: Unscramble CIFAIPC. It names a famous…
why: CIFAIPC rearranges to PACIFIC.

q: Drop the first letter of each. Which one does NOT leave a real word: Blame, Stone, Chair, Plant?
why: Blame→lame, Stone→tone, Chair→hair, but Plant→lant isn't a word.

q: A die shows 1 on top and 2 facing you. You tip it over once, away from you. What's on top now?
why: Tipping away sends the top face to the back and brings the front face (2) up to the top.

q: Three dice are stacked; the top face shows 5. What do the 5 hidden faces (between and below) add up to?
why: Opposite faces sum to 7: the lower two dice hide 7 + 7, and the top die's bottom is 7 − 5 = 2. Total 16.

q: A painted 4×4×4 cube is cut into 64 small cubes. How many have no paint at all?
why: The unpainted cubes form the 2×2×2 core inside: 8.

q: Fold a sheet in half 3 times, punch one hole through all layers, then unfold. How many holes?
why: Each fold doubles the layers: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 layers, so 8 holes.

q: In a mirror, a clock with no numbers appears to read 2:20. What time is it really?
why: A mirror time and the real time add to 12:00, and 12:00 − 2:20 = 9:40.

q: In a non-leap year, January 1 is a Monday. What day is December 31?
why: Dec 31 is 364 days after Jan 1, exactly 52 weeks, so it's also a Monday.

q: What is the most Friday-the-13ths that can happen in one calendar year?
why: Months starting on the same weekday cluster at most 3 to a year, e.g. Feb, Mar and Nov in 2026.

q: A ball dropped from 16 m bounces back to half its height each time. Distance traveled when it lands the 4th time?
why: 16 down, then 8 up and 8 down, 4 up and 4 down, 2 up and 2 down: 16 + 16 + 8 + 4 = 44.

q: A 100 m train at 10 m/s goes through a 200 m tunnel. How long from entering to fully out?
why: The front must travel the tunnel plus its own length: 300 m ÷ 10 m/s = 30 s.

q: 9 identical-looking coins; one is heavier. Fewest balance-scale weighings to be sure which?
why: Weigh 3 vs 3 to find the heavy group of 3, then 1 vs 1 from that group.

q: 100 closed doors. On pass k you toggle every k-th door, for k = 1 to 100. How many end up open?
why: Only perfect squares have an odd number of divisors, so doors 1, 4, 9, …, 100 stay open: 10.

q: 100 players enter a knockout tournament (byes allowed). How many matches to crown a winner?
why: Each match knocks out exactly one player, and 99 must be knocked out.

q: When I was 6, my sister was half my age. Now I'm 70. How old is my sister?
why: She was 3 when I was 6, so she's always 3 years younger: 67.

q: 100 kg of melons are 99% water. They dry until they're 98% water. What do they weigh now?
why: The 1 kg of solids is now 2% of the total, so the total is 50 kg.

q: What comes next: 8, 5, 4, 9, 1, 7, 6, ?
why: The digits are in alphabetical order of their names: eight, five, four, nine, one, seven, six, three.

q: Which is correct: 'egg yolks is white' or 'egg yolks are white'?
why: Egg yolks are yellow, so neither sentence is true.

q: A log is cut into 4 pieces. Each cut takes 3 minutes. How long does it take in total?
why: 4 pieces need only 3 cuts: 3 × 3 = 9.

q: A 10 m fence has a post every 2 m, with posts at both ends. How many posts?
why: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 gaps, and there is one more post than gaps.

q: You read pages 14 to 27 of a book, both included. How many pages did you read?
why: 27 − 14 = 13, plus 1 because both ends count.

q: 12 coins, all nickels or dimes, total exactly $1. How many dimes?
why: 8 dimes (80¢) + 4 nickels (20¢) = 12 coins, $1.

q: One inch is 2.54 cm. How many centimetres are in one foot?
How many square centimetres are in one square metre?
A die shows 1, 2 and 3 on its three visible faces. What do the three hidden faces add up to?
why: All six faces total 21; 21 − 6 = 15.

q: How many edges does a cube have?
why: 4 on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 upright ones.

q: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
why: 2 triangular ends plus 3 rectangular sides.

q: Draw both diagonals in a square. How many triangles of any size can you see?
why: 4 small triangles, plus 4 halves each made of 2 small ones.

q: Flip two fair coins. What is the chance both land heads?
why: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4 (HH out of HH, HT, TH, TT).

q: A fair coin lands heads 5 times in a row. Chance the next flip is heads?
why: Coins have no memory; each flip is still 1/2.

q: Roll one die. What is the chance of getting a number greater than 4?
why: Only 5 and 6 work: 2 out of 6.

q: Roll two dice. Which total is the most likely?
why: 7 can be made 6 ways, more than any other total.

q: Draw one card from a 52-card deck. Chance it's a face card (J, Q or K)?
why: 12 face cards out of 52 = 3/13.

q: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. Take out two at random. Chance both are red?
The 3rd of a month is a Friday. What day is the 24th?
why: The 24th is 21 days later, exactly 3 weeks.

q: What date is exactly 3 weeks after March 25?
why: March 25 + 21 days: 6 days to March 31, then 15 more.

q: How many days are in January, February and March of a non-leap year?
Which of these years was a leap year?
why: Century years are leap years only if divisible by 400.

q: You buy a goat for $6, sell it for $8, buy it back for $10 and sell it for $12. Your profit?
why: You made $2 on each of the two deals.

q: Which deal is cheaper per apple: 3 for $2 or 5 for $3?
why: 60¢ an apple versus about 67¢ an apple.

q: Which of these is divisible by 9?
why: Its digits add to 18, a multiple of 9.

q: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 40?
What is the sum of all the whole numbers from 1 to 20?
Which of these is a perfect square?
What is the last digit of 9 to the power 99?
why: Odd powers of 9 end in 9; even powers end in 1.

q: Which word is spelled wrong in every dictionary?
why: The word 'wrong' is always spelled W-R-O-N-G.

q: How many letters of the alphabet come after T?
why: U, V, W, X, Y and Z.

q: Rearrange the letters of LEMNO. You get a kind of…
why: LEMNO unscrambles to LEMON (or MELON).

q: What starts with E, ends with E, and usually contains only one letter?
why: It holds one letter, as in a piece of mail.

q: Which word contains all five vowels A, E, I, O, U?
why: F-A-C-E-T-I-O-U-S has each vowel once.

q: Which day of the week has the most letters in its name?
why: Wednesday has 9 letters; Thursday and Saturday have 8.

q: Which month has the most letters in its name?
why: September has 9 letters; the others have 8.

q: What is the 13th letter of the alphabet?
why: A-M is the first half of the 26 letters.

q: A woman shoots her husband, holds him underwater, then hangs him up. Later they dine out. How?
why: She shot a photo, developed it in liquid and hung it to dry.

q: What is so fragile that just saying its name breaks it?
why: Speaking the word breaks the silence.

q: A father and son crash. The surgeon says 'I can't operate, he's my son!' Who is the surgeon?
why: The surgeon is a woman: the boy's mum.

q: Which word sounds the same even after you remove four of its five letters?
why: Q-ueue: the letter Q sounds just like 'queue'.

q: If you have it, you want to share it. If you share it, you no longer have it. What is it?
why: Once told, it isn't a secret any more.

q: A cowboy rides into town on Friday, stays three days, and leaves on Friday. How?
why: Friday is the horse's name, not the day.

q: What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
why: Dig more out and the hole grows.

q: Before Mount Everest was discovered, what was the world's tallest mountain?
why: It was still the tallest, just not yet measured.

q: How far can a dog run into a forest?
why: After halfway it is running out of the forest.

q: In a one-storey house where everything is pink, what colour are the stairs?
why: A one-storey house has no stairs.

q: Can a man legally marry his widow's sister?
why: If he has a widow, he has died.

q: A bowl holds six apples. You take away four. How many apples do you have?
why: You have the four you took.

q: An electric train heads north while the wind blows south. Which way does its smoke go?
why: Electric trains don't make smoke.

q: Box A says 'Gold isn't here.' B says 'Gold isn't here.' C says 'It's in B.' Only one is true. Gold is in?
why: Only gold in A leaves exactly one true sign (B's).

q: All bloops are razzies and all razzies are lazzies. Are all bloops lazzies?
why: Bloops sit inside razzies, which sit inside lazzies.

q: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. So do some roses fade quickly?
why: The quick-fading flowers might not include any roses.

q: Jo finishes ahead of Kim but behind Lu. Max beats Lu. Who came last?
why: Order: Max, Lu, Jo, Kim.

q: Knights always tell the truth; knaves always lie. Who could say 'I am a knave'?
why: A knight would be lying; a knave would be telling the truth.

q: Who is your mother's brother's only sister?
why: Your uncle's only sister must be your mum.

q: A is B's brother. B is C's sister. C is D's father. What is A to D?
why: A is a brother of D's father.

q: How many minutes are in one week?
How many hours are in the month of March?
why: 31 days × 24 hours = 744.

q: A leap year is how many weeks long?
You take a pill every other day, starting on the 1st. On what date is your 8th pill?
How many times a day do a clock's hour and minute hands overlap?
why: 11 times every 12 hours; there's no overlap between 11 and 1.

q: What letter comes next: B, E, H, K, ?
why: Each letter jumps 3 places: K + 3 = N.

q: What comes next: 31, 28, 31, 30, 31, ?
why: Days in each month: June has 30.

q: What comes next: 6, 3, 10, 5, 16, 8, ?
why: Halve even numbers; triple odd ones and add 1.

q: How many whole numbers have exactly three digits?
Sam is 3 times as old as Pat. Together they are 48. How old is Sam?
why: Pat is 48 ÷ 4 = 12, so Sam is 36.

q: Three siblings are born 2 years apart. Their ages add up to 33. How old is the oldest?
why: The middle one is 33 ÷ 3 = 11; oldest is 13.

q: A price rises from $40 to $50. What is the percentage increase?
why: The $10 rise is measured against the $40 start.

q: A class has 25 pupils and 60% are girls. How many boys are there?
A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per km. You pay $19. How far did you go?
You have $20 and save $5 every week. After how many weeks will you have $100?
why: You need $80 more: 80 ÷ 5 = 16.

q: Using 1¢, 5¢, 10¢ and 25¢ coins, what's the fewest coins that make 68¢?
A loaf costs $3. A cake costs as much as 4 loaves. What do 2 cakes and 3 loaves cost?
Which distance is the longest?
why: A mile is about 1,609 m; the others are all under 1,560 m.

q: At which temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales read the same?
A recipe needs 3/4 cup of flour for 6 people. How much for 8 people?
why: 1/8 cup per person × 8 = 1 cup.

q: On a 1:50,000 map, two towns are 4 cm apart. How far apart are they really?
What is 50 cm + 300 mm + 0.2 m?
How many rectangles of any size are in a row of 3 squares?
why: 3 singles, 2 doubles and 1 triple.

q: Cutting straight down, with no stacking, what's the most pieces 3 straight cuts can make of a pizza?
why: Each new cut crosses all earlier ones: 1 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 7.

q: Face north. Turn right, turn right again, then turn left. Which way do you face?
why: North → East → South → East.

q: A cube's edges are all doubled in length. Its volume becomes…
What do the interior angles of a hexagon add up to?
Which word looks exactly the same in a mirror held beside it?
why: W and O are symmetric left-to-right; D, B and N are not.

q: What is MCMXC in Roman numerals?
How many 3-cent stamps are in a dozen?
why: A dozen of anything is 12.
